title: Why he enjoyed Germany: Weimar culture and discipline
summary: Briggs liked the congenial, cultured, disciplined Germans of the Weimar era under Stresemann despite financial troubles and inflation.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. I mean, you enjoyed being in Germany at that time. What was nice about it?
The nice thing in Germany was just that the Germans were very congenial.
They were?
They are a very cultured people. They were very congenial. There were no symptoms of the last war, World War I outside of Mrs. Glasner's original feeling, which was a personal thing.

I had a really wonderful time in Germany, and not only I but the orchestra in general, and all the musicians -- we had quite a few French musicians and from everywhere else, in Berlin, and they all had a wonderful time.
Well, because that
Briggs
was the time of the Weimar Republic.
Weimar Republic with Stresemann.
And there was a lot of artistic things going on at that time?

Yes, plenty of them. Although, what would you say, the financial situation in Germany was pretty bad. But we overcame it. We didn't realize the German money had taken a flop, before we went to Germany and while we were with the Syncopated Orchestra in London. That's where half of the German money went. It was that bad. But there was something -- I rather liked the atmosphere in Germany, because in the first place they were disciplined.
They were.
And people can say what they want, but we are disciplined. Anything that has to do with the Anglo-Saxons,
Briggs 183
is disciplined, you see.
Right.
And that's one thing that I admired so much when I got along nicely with them. I had no difficulties at all.
Well, was that when that great inflation was on?
Yes.
And the Mark was just being inflated --
No, that was after.
That was later?

Later. The Mark flopped while we were in England. 'Cause I remember, I remember some of the boys saying, 'You want to get well, go ahead and buy some Marks.' And I, was like a big fool, I bought -- (Laughter). Well, it was just one of those things. I didn't lose much.
